title: Delayed-free tombstone accumulation in multipool prefetching under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Under sustained continuous-batching workloads with KV prefetch enabled, we observe steady GPU resident memory growth that correlates with delayed frees accumulating as "tombstones" in the multipool allocator. This manifests as fragmentation and eventual OOMs for long-running instances.

Symptoms and impact:
- Steady resident growth ~35-70 MB/min on p4d-like instances during mixed small/large batch traffic.
- Out-of-memory only after multi-hour runs; initial latency unaffected but tail latency increases as allocator stalls.
- Affects hosted and dedicated nodes where KV prefetch is active and batch coalescing is enabled.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Start runtime branch with kv-prefetch toggled on (testing config used: PREFETCH_WINDOW=32, PREFETCH_PARALLELISM=4).
2) Replay MixedBatchTraffic workload (mix: 60% small 8-token requests, 40% long 512-token requests) at 300 qps.
3) Observe resident set via nvprof/nvidia-smi and allocator histograms (/metrics/allocators).
4) In problematic runs freed-chunk counters increase but resident pages do not drop; freed objects marked with epoch older than stream-trim window.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- KV prefetch creates transient allocations on background CUDA streams. cudaFreeAsync/free events are being queued on streams that are not observed by the allocator's epoch-trimming pass, leaving freed pages as tombstones tied to stale stream contexts.
- Multipool repooling logic treats these tombstones as in-use for slab residency accounting, preventing coalescing and causing fragmentation.
- Continuous batching increases the rate of short-lived KV allocations and widens the window between allocation and stream completion, amplifying the effect.

What we've tried so far:
- Added synchronous stream-drain after prefetch in a test branch (runtime/pr/12345). Reduced growth to ~5 MB/min but increased latency for prefetch path; unacceptable for SLAs.
- Implemented a reclamation pass that scans for tombstones older than N seconds and forces host-free fallback. This reduced long-run fragmentation in 6-hour runs but introduced non-deterministic stalls under bursty traffic.
- Tuned PREFETCH_WINDOW down to 8 which reduced leak but increased cache-miss rate and downstream latency; customer observable regression in embeddings-heavy workloads.

Proposed mitigations (trade-offs):
- Short-term: implement epoch-aware free notification for background streams so allocator's trim pass accounts for stream completion without synchronizing streams (preferred). Requires adding stream-completion callbacks and tracking per-stream pending frees. Estimated 3-4 pts.
- Medium-term: introduce a lightweight tombstone coalescer that opportunistically merges adjacent freed regions across pools during low load. Lower latency impact but complex to get right with pinned staging buffers. Estimated 5 pts.
- Long-term: redesign prefetch scheduling to favor pinned host staging for very short-lived allocations (avoid device allocation churn). Larger infra + perf trade-offs and likely affects cache hit efficiency.

Artifacts and data:
- Repro pipeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/kv-prefetch-repro
- PR with synchronous-drain experiment: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345
- Reclamation PoC branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/allocator-reclaim-poc
- Confluence notes + allocation traces: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-260117+Tombstone+Investigation
- Grafana dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/kv-alloc/kv-prefetch-allocations

Acceptance criteria for resolution:
- No unexplained resident growth after 24h at 300 qps for the MixedBatchTraffic test with prefetch enabled.
- No increase >5% p99 latency for prefetch path compared to baseline.
- No OOM incidents in 7-day soak on dedicated pool with mixed traffic.

Next steps (owners):
- Marco A. (assignee): implement epoch-aware free notification and unit tests (ETA: 2026-03-09).
- Priya Singh (reviewer): validate perf impact on prefetch latency (ETA: 2026-03-09).
- SRE (monitoring): run 48h soak on dedicated staging and report regressions (ETA: 2026-03-12).
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Initial report after two customer incidents where long-running dedicated nodes hit OOMs. Pinned down to prefetch-enabled stacks. Attached early traces and nvprof captures.

2026-02-20 - Marco Alvarez: Reproduced locally using MixedBatchTraffic repro harness. Confirmed freed-chunk counter increases but resident memory does not reclaim. Stack trace shows frees queued on stream 7 repeatedly.
2026-02-22 - Marco Alvarez: Experimented with synchronous stream drain (runtime PR 12345). Memory stabilizes but end-to-end latency for prefetch increases ~12% p95. Not acceptable in hosted tier.
2026-02-24 - Priya Singh: Review notes on PR 12345: prefer not to add broad synchronization. Suggest exploring stream-completion callbacks or polling-based acknowledgment in allocator to avoid stall.

2026-02-25 - Marco Alvarez: Built PoC: allocator-reclaim-poc. Uses host-side lightweight fence polling to mark tombstones reclaimable once stream reports completion. In 6h run, growth reduced by ~80% and no OOM. Need more robust tests for corner cases.
2026-02-27 - Design/Docs: Added Confluence doc with allocation timelines and annotated nvprof flame graphs. https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-260117+Tombstone+Investigation

2026-02-28 - Performance team: Ran 2h A/B with PREFETCH_WINDOW=16 vs 32. Observed cache-hit drop with smaller window; trade-off shown in dashboard link. Recommended implement epoch aware free as priority.
2026-03-01 - Marco Alvarez: Opening ENG follow-up tasks: create unit tests for stream-callback integration and add metric for tombstone-count (kv.alloc.tombstones).
